Development economics

Development economics studies how economies and living standards change over time and why outcomes differ across people and places. It covers questions involving poverty, education, health, labour markets, firms, institutions, and public policy.

Modern development economics combines economic theory with empirical research. Household surveys, administrative data, field experiments, and other methods are used to understand mechanisms and evaluate interventions.
